claims.claim: Smak og distinksjon: Smak analyseres som sosial praksis knyttet til klasseposisjon og symbolske grenser.

source_evidence.locator: Distinction, 1984 English translation excerpt, pp. 1–7 and 28–33; cultural practices, education/social origin, and taste as a marker of class

claims.claim: Kulturell kapital: Kunnskap, disposisjoner og legitime kulturformer kan fungere som ressurser når et felt anerkjenner dem.

source_evidence.locator: Bourdieu, The Forms of Capital, 1986, pp. 243–244; cultural capital as field-dependent capital, its embodied/objectified/institutionalized forms, acquisition through time and differential transmission

claims.claim: Klassifikasjonskamp: Grupper konkurrerer om retten til å definere legitimt og illegitimt.

source_evidence.locator: Bourdieu, Social Space and Symbolic Power, Sociological Theory 7(1), pp. 20–22; symbolic struggles over legitimate vision/division, categories of perception and the power to impose classifications

claims.claim: Dramaturgisk analyse: Sosiale møter kan analyseres som opptredener med publikum og situasjonsdefinisjoner.

source_evidence.locator: Goffman 1959, Introduction pp. 1–5 and Performances excerpt pp. 22–30; interaction as performance before observers, expressive front, and definition of the situation

claims.claim: Inntrykksstyring: Aktører påvirker hvordan andre fortolker situasjonen gjennom uttrykk og informasjonskontroll.

source_evidence.locator: Goffman 1959, Introduction pp. 2–4; expressions given and given off, and influence over others’ definition of the situation and responsive treatment

claims.claim: Opptredende team: Flere aktører kan samarbeide om å opprettholde samme situasjonsdefinisjon.

source_evidence.locator: Goffman 1959, Conclusion/The Framework, pp. 238–239; a team of performers cooperates to present one definition of the situation, with solidarity, shared secrets and coordinated front/back regions sustaining the performance

claims.claim: Sosiogenese og psykogenese: Langsiktige sosiale avhengigheter kobles til endringer i selvkontroll og følelsesregulering.

source_evidence.locator: Four Interviews with Norbert Elias, ‘In reality, we are all late barbarians’ (1989), passages on civilisation, state formation and self-regulation; Elias links civilising processes to state formation and describes self-regulation adapting to higher levels of social integration

claims.claim: Statsdannelse og monopol: Konsentrasjon av skatte- og voldsmonopol endrer maktbalanser og atferdskrav.

source_evidence.locator: Elias, On the Monopoly Mechanism, in On Civilization, Power, and Knowledge, p. 139; taxation/property income is concentrated in a central social authority, whose financial means maintain its monopoly of military force, while that force in turn maintains the monopoly of taxation

claims.claim: Interdependens og figurasjoner: Samfunn forstås som dynamiske nett av gjensidig avhengige aktører.

source_evidence.locator: Four Interviews with Norbert Elias, ‘In reality, we are all late barbarians’ (1989), discussion of European integration; Elias states that social strata and states are dependent on one another and explicitly describes increasing interdependence across social strata

claims.claim: Disiplinær makt: Makt virker gjennom ordninger av tid, rom, kropp, trening og inspeksjon.

source_evidence.locator: Discipline and Punish, Part III, Docile Bodies, pp. 135–141 in the cited English edition; discipline works through detailed control of bodies, partitioning of space, codification of time and movement, exercise, supervision and the production of docile bodies

claims.claim: Normalisering og eksamen: Måling, rangering og dokumentasjon kan produsere korrigerende normer.

source_evidence.locator: Discipline and Punish, Panopticism, pp. 195–228 in the cited 1995 Vintage edition; normal/abnormal division, techniques for measuring, supervising and correcting, rigorous classifications, assessment and behavioral correction

claims.claim: Panoptisisme: Asymmetrisk synlighet kan bidra til selvregulering når observasjon er mulig, men usikker.

source_evidence.locator: Panopticism, pp. 195–228 in the cited 1995 Vintage edition

claims.claim: Forestilte fellesskap: Nasjonen er forestilt fordi medlemmer opplever et felles vi uten å møte de fleste andre.

source_evidence.locator: Imagined Communities, revised edition, pp. 5–7; nation defined as an imagined political community, with members holding an image of communion despite never knowing or meeting most fellow-members

claims.claim: Trykkapitalisme: Trykte markeder og standardiserte språk bidrar til nye former for kollektiv identifikasjon.

source_evidence.locator: Imagined Communities, Chapter 3 excerpt published by Verso, The Origins of National Consciousness; capitalism and mechanical print assemble vernaculars into print-languages, create unified fields of exchange and communication, and form nationally imagined communities

claims.claim: Homogen, tom tid: Moderne medier og kalendere muliggjør forestillingen om samtidige liv i samme historiske tid.

source_evidence.locator: Imagined Communities, Chapter 2, pp. 24–26; homogeneous empty time is simultaneity measured by clock and calendar, while novel and newspaper provide technical means to represent simultaneous lives in the imagined national community

claims.claim: Teknologisk akselerasjon: Transport, kommunikasjon og produksjon kan utføres raskere og endre forventninger.

source_evidence.locator: Chapter 3: Technical Acceleration and the Revolutionizing of the Space-Time Regime, pp. 97–107

claims.claim: Akselerasjon av sosial endring: Institusjoner og forventninger kan få kortere stabilitetsperioder.

source_evidence.locator: Chapter 4: Slipping Slopes: The Acceleration of Social Change and the Increase of Contingency, pp. 108–119

claims.claim: Akselerert livstempo: Flere handlinger og opplevelser kan presses inn i samme tidsrom.

source_evidence.locator: Chapter 5: The Acceleration of the Pace of Life and Paradoxes in the Experience of Time, pp. 120–148

claims.claim: Spor assosiasjoner: Forbindelser undersøkes empirisk fremfor å bruke 'det sosiale' som ferdig forklaring.

source_evidence.locator: Latour, On using ANT for studying information systems, pp. 69–71; actor-networks are captured by following transformations and writing the network as it is traced, with no claim allowed where actors leave no trace

claims.claim: Mediatorer og intermediærer: Noen ledd transporterer relativt stabilt, mens andre transformerer det som passerer.

source_evidence.locator: Latour, On using ANT for studying information systems, pp. 69–70; no transparent medium, only mediators, with information treated as transformation/translation rather than unchanged transport

claims.claim: Menneskelige og ikke-menneskelige aktanter: Teknologier, dokumenter og materialitet kan muliggjøre og begrense handling.

source_evidence.locator: Latour, On using ANT for studying information systems, pp. 72–73; people, objects and sites enter the account as actors when they make a difference, while passive intermediaries/place-holders are rejected

claims.claim: Økonomiens innleiring: Økonomiske relasjoner forstås som historisk innvevd i sosiale og politiske institusjoner.

source_evidence.locator: The Great Transformation, Chapter IV: Societies and Economic Systems, pp. 46–49; economy submerged in social relationships, with production/distribution organized through social interests, reciprocity, redistribution and institutional patterns

claims.claim: Fiktive varer: Arbeid, jord og penger behandles som varer selv om de ikke er produsert for salg som ordinære varer.

source_evidence.locator: Chapter 6: The Self-Regulating Market and the Fictitious Commodities: Labor, Land, and Money

claims.claim: Dobbelbevegelsen: Markedsutvidelse ledsages av politiske og sosiale forsøk på beskyttelse mot virkninger.

source_evidence.locator: The Great Transformation, Chapter 11: Man, Nature, and Productive Organization, pp. 130–133; the double movement is defined as continuous market expansion/economic liberalism opposed by a protective countermovement conserving people, nature and productive organization

claims.claim: Labor, work og action: Arendt skiller livsopprettholdelse, fremstilling av en varig verden og politisk handling.

source_evidence.locator: Arendt, Labor, Work, Action (1987), pp. 29–30 and 35–39; labor sustains biological life, work fabricates a durable human world, and action organizes living together and discloses agents through word and deed

claims.claim: Pluralitet: Politisk handling forutsetter både felles verden og reell forskjellighet mellom aktører.

source_evidence.locator: Arendt, Labor, Work, Action (1987), p. 39; human activities are conditioned by plurality, while action and speech specifically depend on living among distinct equals and insert the actor into an already shared world

claims.claim: Natalitet og begynnelse: Handling knyttes til kapasiteten for å begynne noe nytt i en felles verden.

source_evidence.locator: Arendt, Labor, Work, Action (1987), pp. 39 and 41–42; action is likened to a second birth, its impulse springs from the beginning introduced by birth, and each human birth carries the capacity to begin something new
